claims.claim: CCS deployment of4–10Gt/y by2050 requires substantial expansion and realistic geological constraints.
claims.assessment: Historical projection and growth context; not independently checked deployment forecasts.

claims.claim: Hydrocarbon flow and well-construction analogues favor some regions and imply10000–14000 offshore wells.
claims.assessment: An industry analogue, not a validated physical-rate or project-inventory model.

claims.claim: Economic and growth models can constrain deployment but omit some reservoir physics.
claims.assessment: Original model assumptions/results unverified; no wholesale invalidation of economic models inferred.

claims.claim: Pressure buildup and injectivity can limit field/regional storage, with seismic, deformation and leakage risks.
claims.assessment: Mechanistic motivation, not quantified failure/leak probability or a complete site safety assessment.

claims.claim: Permits constrain maximum operating pressures.
claims.assessment: The cited2023NSTA original and actual permit definitions are unverified; no pressure datum or universal limit inferred.

claims.claim: Numerical cases can be too expensive for global use, motivating analytical approximations.
claims.assessment: Source-method context, not a reproduced accuracy/performance comparison.

claims.claim: CO2BLOCK superposes nonlinear single-well solutions and can correct superposition error.
claims.assessment: Original derivations/code and option settings remain unverified locally.

claims.claim: Each modeled injection point can represent several nearby wells; the site ceiling is5Mt/y.
claims.assessment: Do not turn this into a per-well injection limit or actual well count.

claims.claim: The model uses homogeneous basins, uniform Cartesian sites and equal constant rates.
claims.assessment: No staged development, heterogeneous compartment geometry, pressure management or field-specific controls are reproduced.

claims.claim: CO2BLOCK estimates pressure and a notional plume but not migration/trapping-limited capacity or retention extents.
claims.assessment: Pressure feasibility is distinct from permanent containment; the Figure1geometric constraint needs its original definitions.

claims.claim: Seven inputs and open/closed boundaries are needed, with other properties defaulted when absent.
claims.assessment: Native defaults, reference pressure solution, EOS and stress conventions are unavailable locally; all basins are set closed here.

claims.claim: Outputs include pressure, sustained site rate and cumulative resource at chosen durations/spacings.
claims.assessment: Horizon-specific constant-rate cases do not form one time-varying deployment path.

claims.claim: Multistratigraphic properties are arithmetically averaged and faults/compartments ignored across248basins.
claims.assessment: Explicit coarse scope; national figures are not site-specific annual service or validated uncertainty estimates.

claims.claim: The scheme contains764basins, with commercial petroleum data and some USGS inputs.
claims.assessment: The public USGS lineage and exact input subset remain unverified; commercial data are not an open reproducible basin dataset.

claims.claim: More than80000petroleum reservoir records and well locations inform properties and scenarios.
claims.assessment: Repeated/selectively sampled hydrocarbon data are not an unbiased independent sample of saline aquifers.

claims.claim: Filtering top depth>800m is said to ensure supercritical CO₂.
claims.assessment: Depth alone does not establish temperature and pressure state; native P/T/EOS/defaults are needed to verify actual cases.

claims.claim: A straddling basin is assigned wholly to the country/continent with most basin area.
claims.assessment: This aggregation differs from territorial resource allocation and explains part of international differences; no ownership inference.

claims.claim: Twelve scenarios combine4/25/100/400sites and5/15/30km spacing.
claims.assessment: All twelve patterns are preserved with technical ceilings only; no native pressure-limited rates are calculated.

claims.claim: Scenario3 resembles Endurance;30km trades interference against fit, and400sites resembles542NorthSea fields.
claims.assessment: These analogues do not establish field feasibility, engineering completion or actual project numbers.

claims.claim: Scenario12 fits20of265basins described as having sufficient data.
claims.assessment: The265population is not reconciled with248modelled basins and992four-site points; no filter is guessed.

claims.claim: ScenarioM selects each basin's greatest resource from the twelve patterns, separately at30/80years.
claims.assessment: A finite candidate maximum, rather than proof of an unrestricted physical or economically achievable global optimum.

claims.claim: The history filter excludes basins with insufficient hydrocarbon wells, leaving204basins and about17%average resource reduction.
claims.assessment: The boundary is stated as fewer-than100excluded versus more-than100eligible elsewhere. Petroleum sampling already favors explored basins.

claims.claim: BandA/Breadiness uses ten countries and sharply lowers global resource estimates.
claims.assessment: Historic2015/2018index scenarios, not current readiness or a causal ranking of every CCS constraint.

claims.claim: Pressure-limited cases benefit from larger spacing; site-limited cases saturate at5Mt/y/site.
claims.assessment: Classification is conditional on chosen patterns and includes low-kh limits; site-limited does not mean all geological risks absent.

claims.claim: European workflow goes from72basins/8739records/6673fields to7046depth-filtered records and36usable basins.
claims.assessment: Repeated field/stratum entries and variable-specific missingness require native weights/properties. No European model case was independently rerun.

claims.claim: No European basin fits Scenario12; Central/NorthernNorthSea choose10 and SouthernNorthSea8.
claims.assessment: Case selection claims, rather than native per-basin optimization reproduced from data.

claims.claim: Deployment comparisons use120Gtcumulative,5.6Gt/y and10Gt/y benchmarks.
claims.assessment: Convert rates to cumulative mass only under an explicit flat-rate duration; these are not actual IAM trajectories.

claims.claim: Asia often supplies the largest resource; Brazil, Australia and selected other countries rank high.
claims.assessment: Depends on scenario, data coverage and majority-basin assignment; no current nationally available storage service inferred.

claims.claim: ScenarioM gives3640Gt/30years and5630Gt/80years using a reported73508sites.
claims.assessment: Rounded rates121and70Gt/y agree with mass/duration. The single site-count horizon is not specified, while Figure3patterns change.

claims.claim: Pressure constraints increase with site number and decrease with spacing; scenarios7/10are100%pressure-limited.
claims.assessment: Scenario comparisons need feasibility/weighting; these are not probabilities that storage fails.

claims.claim: Scenario3has about30%pressure-limited basins/resource and70%site-limited resource.
claims.assessment: The prose changes between basin counts and resource shares. Figure7labels global resource; exact denominator, duration and filters need clarification.

claims.claim: Regional site-limited examples include LosAngeles, Brazil/Amazonas, African basins, NorthSea/Aegean and Asian basins.
claims.assessment: SixFigure8panels use different scenarios, horizons and diameter scales; do not compare circle area as mass.

claims.claim: LosAngeles provides96%of site-limited storage in Scenario4after30years.
claims.assessment: This is not96%of total US resource or a safety/retention probability.

claims.claim: Only scenarios11andMmeet10Gt/y in readiness-band cases.
claims.assessment: The30-year panel supports this; the80-year panel visibly places onlyMabove800Gt. Preserve the mid-century scope instead of extending the claim to both horizons.

claims.claim: Scenarios11andMhave91%and81%of resource pressure-limited.
claims.assessment: Figure7is globally weighted and does not specify duration/readiness-filter correspondence; native subset arrays are required.

claims.claim: Volumetric estimates use0.5–4%efficiency and usually exceed pressure-limited resources.
claims.assessment: Different geology, geography, methods and durations prevent attributing every difference solely to pressure.

claims.claim: Australia471Gtversus90.2, USA8613Gtversus699after80years.
claims.assessment: Reported comparisons, not independently validated national data; Australian horizon and common basis need native arrays.

claims.claim: PowderRiver3.2Gt agrees with a prior dynamic estimate, but can fill in80years here.
claims.assessment: The original uses different pressure/migration/time conditions, including101years; equality is not independent validation.

claims.claim: UK71.2Gt is6.4below77.6; Norway80.7is close to79.4.
claims.assessment: Literal differences checked. Data sampling and whole-basin country assignment, including43GtCormorant, prevent a like-for-like validation.

claims.claim: Prior selected UK offshore estimates give25sites/140Gtwith about-order-of-magnitude uncertainty.
claims.assessment: This uncertainty is referenced, not independently propagated or calibrated for the global study.

claims.claim: Brazil/Oman/Saudi and21African countries lack comparable entries or surveys in the cited catalogue.
claims.assessment: Historical catalogue-coverage claims; absence in that catalogue is not proof no public survey exists today.

claims.claim: 5Mt/y/site divided by0.57Mt/y/well is roughly nine wells per site, giving1100–1600site analogues.
claims.assessment: An average-rate conversion, not actual required wells or a universal physical upper bound.

claims.claim: NorthSea16809registered wells corresponds to roughly1900site analogues.
claims.assessment: No evidence that historical wells are suitable, intact or available for CCS.

claims.claim: Scenarios1–3have992sites; Scenario3stores128Gt/30years and meets120Gt.
claims.assessment: Arithmetic supports248four-site basins and4.27Gt/y, rather than a10Gt/y target.

claims.claim: Scenario11has50800sites;73508Msites imply18377four-site projects or661572nine-well equivalents.
claims.assessment: The products agree, but the analogues and horizon must remain explicit; these are not a construction schedule.

claims.claim: The well analogue exceeds two-thirds of920000petroleum wells.
claims.assessment: Count ratio is about71.9%, without demonstrating feasibility, integrity or actual CCS well demand.

claims.claim: The5Mt/y/site ceiling might be conservative relative to some large actual/planned projects.
claims.assessment: HistoricalLula/Bluebonnet/Exxonexamples differ in date, scope and status; no current-operation verification performed.

claims.claim: Global outputs may vary by about one order of magnitude like the prior CO2BLOCK study.
claims.assessment: Borrowed sensitivity scale, rather than an empirical confidence interval or own probabilistic propagation.

claims.claim: Immediate development and proven hydrocarbon properties make the results optimistic; legacy wells add risk.
claims.assessment: The38%integrity survey is not a global leak/failure probability or retained-carbon fraction.

claims.claim: Ignoring sealing compartments can overestimate feasible basin resource, requiring separate injection sites.
claims.assessment: Explicit authors’ limitation; no actual compartment model or annual field control is reproduced.

claims.claim: Results are described as upper bounds and not designed to identify storage sites.
claims.assessment: A scenario assessment with omitted constraints, not a mathematically proven bound across all possible pressure-management designs.

claims.claim: Monitoring and brine extraction can mitigate pressure but add costs and were not modeled.
claims.assessment: No corresponding energy, treatment/disposal, environmental or lifecycle inventory supplied.

claims.claim: History-restrictedMresource is3000/4500Gt, readiness-restrictedM780/1177Gt.
claims.assessment: Mass/duration supports100/56and26/15Gt/yrounded quotes. These are separately optimized cases, not one rate history.

claims.claim: Readiness-constrained target cases require over50000sites and lower targets at least20000sites.
claims.assessment: Scope, horizon, target and scenario arrays must be stated; no actual project construction or well program is reproduced.

claims.claim: A disclaimer separates these estimates from WoodMackenzie's LensCarbon methodology.
claims.assessment: Preserve this distinction; input provenance does not establish identical methods or endorse a commercial product.

claims.claim: The authors do not have permission to share data; supplements/list of basins are referenced.
claims.assessment: This is a documented public method with restricted underlying data, not an acquired reproducible public reservoir dataset.

claims.claim: Three authors, NERC/Shell funding, commercial data support and an editor-in-chief interest are disclosed.
claims.assessment: Provenance only, with no unsupported misconduct or independence conclusion.

claims.claim: All68bibliography entries define the model, data and context lineage.
claims.assessment: Native lines and cross-pageIPCC2018continuation preserved; all originals remain unverified and no new original-passage edge is claimed.

claims.claim: Paper1implication: global pressure-aware assessment is existing methodological precedent.
claims.assessment: Keep field-level service, uncertainty and storage containment distinct from published global upper-bound resources.

claims.claim: Paper1implication: constant horizon rates, multi-well sites and pressure-resource shares cannot be pooled with field limits.
claims.assessment: 53diagnostics, twelve design rows and synthetic mathematical components are not native global CO2BLOCK reproduction.

claims.claim: Paper1implication: this paper does not close public-data, capture-utility or retained-carbon requirements.
claims.assessment: No accepted operating/GHG input is added; restricted data and missing defaults/code/results remain explicit.
